title: Mapping External Cohorts onto Reference INTERACT GNN Embeddings
text: analyzing external validation query cohort, often useful map new samples onto embedding space clusters defined reference cohort rather clustering new cohort separately. INTERACT, RunInteractAutoencoder() supports reference--query encoding interact.results.query argument. Graph Autoencoder (GINEConv) trained reference cohort, query cohort scaled encoded using frozen reference scaler model weights. vignette demonstrates : Generate reference (\(n = 100\)) query (\(n = 50\)) RunInteract() results encode shared GNN latent space using RunInteractAutoencoder(). Assign query samples reference clusters (C1, C2, …) using \(k\)-Nearest Neighbors (\(k\)-NN). Project query samples onto reference UMAP coordinates plot cohorts side side.

title: Mapping External Cohorts onto Reference INTERACT GNN Embeddings
code: # Load required packages library(INTERACT) library(dplyr) library(class) library(umap) library(ggplot2) library(ggsci) library(patchwork)

what: 2. Generate Reference and Query INTERACT Results
title: Mapping External Cohorts onto Reference INTERACT GNN Embeddings
text: Using simulation setup first vignette, generate reference cohort (ref.results, \(n = 100\)) independent query cohort (query.results, \(n = 50\)). query cohort, set run.autoencoder = FALSE RunInteract() interactions encoded jointly reference cohort next step.
code: # Define shared gene symbols and simulation helper genes = c(   "IL6", "IL6R", "IL6ST", "IFNG", "IFNGR1", "IFNGR2", "CD274", "PDCD1",   "CXCL12", "CXCR4", "TNF", "TNFRSF1A", "TGFB1", "TGFBR1", "TGFBR2",   "CCL2", "CCR2", "CXCL9", "CXCL10", "CXCR3", "ICAM1", "ITGAL", "ITGB2",   "STAT1", "STAT3", "JAK1", "JAK2", "IRF1", "SOCS3", "NFKB1", "NFKBIA",   "RELB", "SMAD2", "SMAD3", "JUN", "FOS", "MYC", "AKT1", "PIK3CA", "PTEN" )  simulate.cohort = function(n.samples, prefix, seed) {   set.seed(seed)   sample.states = sample(1:5, n.samples, replace = TRUE)    sim.pop = function(pop.offset) {     mat = matrix(runif(n.samples * length(genes), min = 1, max = 4), nrow = n.samples, ncol = length(genes))     for (i in seq_len(n.samples)) {       active.idx = ((sample.states[i] + pop.offset) %% 5) * 8 + (1:8)       active.idx = active.idx[active.idx <= length(genes)]       mat[i, active.idx] = mat[i, active.idx] + runif(length(active.idx), min = 4, max = 7)     }     rownames(mat) = paste0(prefix, "_", seq_len(n.samples))     colnames(mat) = genes     return(mat)   }    modalities = list(     `T cells` = sim.pop(1),     `Macrophages` = sim.pop(2),     `Tumor` = sim.pop(3)   )    cnv = matrix(pmax(0.5, rnorm(n.samples * length(genes), mean = 2.0, sd = 0.5)), nrow = n.samples)   rownames(cnv) = paste0(prefix, "_", seq_len(n.samples))   colnames(cnv) = genes    snv = matrix(     sample(c(-1, 0, 1), n.samples * length(genes), replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.05, 0.85, 0.10)),     nrow = n.samples   )   rownames(snv) = paste0(prefix, "_", seq_len(n.samples))   colnames(snv) = genes    return(list(modalities = modalities, cnv = cnv, snv = snv)) }  # Run INTERACT on the reference cohort (n = 100) and query cohort (n = 50) n.ref = 100 n.query = 50  ref.sim = simulate.cohort(n.samples = n.ref, prefix = "Ref", seed = 42) query.sim = simulate.cohort(n.samples = n.query, prefix = "Query", seed = 123)  ref.results = RunInteract(   nontumor.matrices = ref.sim$modalities[c("T cells", "Macrophages")],   tumor.matrix = ref.sim$modalities[["Tumor"]],   snv.matrix = ref.sim$snv,   cnv.matrix = ref.sim$cnv,   n.cores = 1 )  # Set run.autoencoder = FALSE to skip training a separate standalone GNN on the # query cohort, since query interactions will be encoded using the reference GNN in Step 3 query.results = RunInteract(   nontumor.matrices = query.sim$modalities[c("T cells", "Macrophages")],   tumor.matrix = query.sim$modalities[["Tumor"]],   snv.matrix = query.sim$snv,   cnv.matrix = query.sim$cnv,   run.autoencoder = FALSE,   n.cores = 1 )

what: 3. Encode Query Cohort into Reference GNN Space
title: Mapping External Cohorts onto Reference INTERACT GNN Embeddings
text: Next, pass ref.results query.results RunInteractAutoencoder(). returns list containing $reference (reference embeddings) $query (query embeddings projected frozen reference encoder). also retrieve reference Louvain cluster assignments ref.results label C1, C2, etc.
code: # Jointly encode reference and query cohorts in a shared GNN space ae.out = RunInteractAutoencoder(   interact.results = ref.results,   interact.results.query = query.results )  # Attach reference cluster labels (formatted as C1, C2, ...) to reference embeddings ref.cluster.df = ref.results$precompute$sample.coords.base |>   dplyr::select(sample, cluster) |>   dplyr::mutate(cluster = sub("^Cluster ", "C", cluster))  cluster.levels = paste0("C", sort( as.integer(sub("^C", "", unique(ref.cluster.df$cluster))) )) n.clusters = length(cluster.levels)  ref.embeddings = ae.out$reference |>   dplyr::inner_join(ref.cluster.df, by = "sample") |>   dplyr::mutate(cluster = factor(cluster, levels = cluster.levels))  query.embeddings = ae.out$query  # Prepare training (reference) and test (query) matrices dim.cols = grep("^GNN\\.Dim\\.", colnames(ref.embeddings), value = TRUE)  train.x = as.matrix(ref.embeddings[, dim.cols]) rownames(train.x) = ref.embeddings$sample train.y = ref.embeddings$cluster  test.x = as.matrix(query.embeddings[, dim.cols]) rownames(test.x) = query.embeddings$sample

what: 4. Assign Query Clusters via k-Nearest Neighbors (\(k = 5\))
title: Mapping External Cohorts onto Reference INTERACT GNN Embeddings
text: classify query sample majority vote 5 nearest reference neighbors GNN embedding space. Setting prob = TRUE records fraction neighbors supporting predicted cluster (prediction.confidence).
code: # Predict query cluster membership via 5-NN majority vote set.seed(42) k.val = 5 pred.y = class::knn(   train = train.x,   test = test.x,   cl = train.y,   k = k.val,   prob = TRUE )  # Summarize predicted clusters and voting confidence query.predictions = data.frame(   sample = query.embeddings$sample,   cluster = factor(pred.y, levels = cluster.levels),   prediction.confidence = attr(pred.y, "prob") )  head(query.predictions) #>     sample cluster prediction.confidence #> 1  Query_1      C3                   0.8 #> 2 Query_10      C2                   1.0 #> 3 Query_11      C2                   1.0 #> 4 Query_12      C2                   0.8 #> 5 Query_13      C3                   0.8 #> 6 Query_14      C1                   1.0

what: 5. Project Query Cohort onto Reference UMAP Space
title: Mapping External Cohorts onto Reference INTERACT GNN Embeddings
text: fit UMAP reference embeddings (train.x) use stats::predict() project query embeddings (test.x) onto 2D coordinate system.
code: # Fit UMAP model on reference embeddings set.seed(42) umap.model = umap::umap(   train.x,   n_neighbors = 15,   min_dist = 0.1,   random_state = 42 )  ref.umap = data.frame(   sample = ref.embeddings$sample,   cluster = train.y,   UMAP1 = umap.model$layout[, 1],   UMAP2 = umap.model$layout[, 2],   cohort = "Reference" )  # Project query embeddings onto reference UMAP space query.coords = stats::predict(umap.model, test.x) query.umap = data.frame(   sample = query.predictions$sample,   cluster = query.predictions$cluster,   UMAP1 = query.coords[, 1],   UMAP2 = query.coords[, 2],   cohort = "Query" )  # Combine coordinates for plotting all.umap = dplyr::bind_rows(ref.umap, query.umap) x.limits = range(all.umap$UMAP1) y.limits = range(all.umap$UMAP2)

what: 6. Visualize Reference and Projected Query Cohorts
title: Mapping External Cohorts onto Reference INTERACT GNN Embeddings
text: Finally, plot reference cohort alongside projected query samples overlaid greyed-reference coordinates.
code: # Define cluster color palette and shared theme cluster.colors = rev(ggsci::pal_npg()(n.clusters)) names(cluster.colors) = cluster.levels  umap.theme = ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11) +   ggplot2::theme(     plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 11, face = "plain", hjust = 0.5, color = "black"),     legend.position = "top",     legend.title = ggplot2::element_blank(),     legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9, face = "plain", color = "black"),     axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(color = "black", face = "plain"),     axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(color = "black", face = "plain")   )  # Panel A: Reference cohort UMAP plot.ref = ggplot2::ggplot(   all.umap |> dplyr::filter(cohort == "Reference"),   ggplot2::aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = cluster) ) +   ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.85) +   ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = cluster.colors, drop = FALSE) +   ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = x.limits, ylim = y.limits) +   ggplot2::labs(     title = paste0("Reference Cohort (n = ", n.ref, ")"),     x = "UMAP 1",     y = "UMAP 2"   ) +   umap.theme +   ggplot2::guides(color = ggplot2::guide_legend(nrow = 1))  # Panel B: Projected query cohort overlaid on reference background plot.query = ggplot2::ggplot(   all.umap |> dplyr::filter(cohort == "Query"),   ggplot2::aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = cluster) ) +   ggplot2::geom_point(     data = all.umap |> dplyr::filter(cohort == "Reference"),     ggplot2::aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2),     color = "grey85",     size = 1.5,     inherit.aes = FALSE   ) +   ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.9) +   ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = cluster.colors, drop = FALSE) +   ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = x.limits, ylim = y.limits) +   ggplot2::labs(     title = paste0("Projected Query Cohort (n = ", n.query, ")"),     x = "UMAP 1",     y = "UMAP 2"   ) +   umap.theme +   ggplot2::guides(color = ggplot2::guide_legend(nrow = 1))  # Combine panels with shared legend combined.plot = (plot.ref | plot.query) +   patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") +   patchwork::plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &   ggplot2::theme(     legend.position = "top",     plot.tag = ggplot2::element_text(size = 13, face = "plain", color = "black")   )  combined.plot

title: INTERACT Analysis with Simulated Data
text: vignette walks standard INTERACT workflow using simulated data. generate expression matrices three cell populations (T cells, Macrophages, Tumor) along tumor somatic copy number variants (CNV) single-nucleotide variants (SNV), score intercellular communication train Graph Autoencoder RunInteract(), visualize resulting signaling networks.

title: INTERACT Analysis with Simulated Data
code: # Load required packages library(INTERACT) library(dplyr) library(igraph) library(ggplot2) library(ggraph) library(visNetwork)

title: INTERACT Analysis with Simulated Data
text: cell population represented numeric matrix samples rows gene symbols columns. Input expression matrices contain non-negative, log-transformed values (\(\log_2(\text{CPM} + 1)\)).
code: # Define cohort size and gene symbols spanning ligands, receptors, and downstream pathways n.samples = 100 genes = c(   "IL6", "IL6R", "IL6ST", "IFNG", "IFNGR1", "IFNGR2", "CD274", "PDCD1",   "CXCL12", "CXCR4", "TNF", "TNFRSF1A", "TGFB1", "TGFBR1", "TGFBR2",   "CCL2", "CCR2", "CXCL9", "CXCL10", "CXCR3", "ICAM1", "ITGAL", "ITGB2",   "STAT1", "STAT3", "JAK1", "JAK2", "IRF1", "SOCS3", "NFKB1", "NFKBIA",   "RELB", "SMAD2", "SMAD3", "JUN", "FOS", "MYC", "AKT1", "PIK3CA", "PTEN" ) set.seed(42)  # Simulate log-scale expression matrices with 5 underlying signaling states sample.states = sample(1:5, n.samples, replace = TRUE)  sim.expression = function(n, g, pop.offset) {   mat = matrix(runif(n * length(g), min = 1, max = 4), nrow = n, ncol = length(g))   for (i in seq_len(n)) {     active.idx = ((sample.states[i] + pop.offset) %% 5) * 8 + (1:8)     active.idx = active.idx[active.idx <= length(g)]     mat[i, active.idx] = mat[i, active.idx] + runif(length(active.idx), min = 4, max = 7)   }   rownames(mat) = paste0("Sample_", seq_len(n))   colnames(mat) = g   return(mat) }  modalities = list(   `T cells` = sim.expression(n.samples, genes, pop.offset = 1),   `Macrophages` = sim.expression(n.samples, genes, pop.offset = 2),   `Tumor` = sim.expression(n.samples, genes, pop.offset = 3) )

title: INTERACT Analysis with Simulated Data
text: Next, simulate gene-level copy number somatic mutation matrices tumor population. Copy number values centered 2.0 (diploid), somatic mutations encoded 1 (activating), -1 (inactivating), 0 (wild type).
code: # Simulate continuous CNV matrix centered at diploid (2.0) cnv = matrix(pmax(0.5, rnorm(n.samples * length(genes), mean = 2.0, sd = 0.5)), nrow = n.samples) rownames(cnv) = paste0("Sample_", seq_len(n.samples)) colnames(cnv) = genes  # Simulate directional SNV matrix (-1 = inactivating, 0 = wild type, 1 = activating) snv = matrix(   sample(c(-1, 0, 1), n.samples * length(genes), replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.05, 0.85, 0.10)),   nrow = n.samples ) rownames(snv) = paste0("Sample_", seq_len(n.samples)) colnames(snv) = genes

title: INTERACT Analysis with Simulated Data
text: pass non-tumor expression list, tumor expression matrix, tumor genomic matrices RunInteract(). default, RunInteract() queries OmniPath intercellular database, computes pathway program weights, trains multi-channel Graph Autoencoder, identifies sample clusters.
code: # Run the full INTERACT pipeline results = RunInteract(   nontumor.matrices = modalities[c("T cells", "Macrophages")],   tumor.matrix = modalities[["Tumor"]],   snv.matrix = snv,   cnv.matrix = cnv,   n.cores = 1 )

title: INTERACT Analysis with Simulated Data
text: BuildGraph() constructs igraph network selected sample, can plotted interactively PlotVisNetwork() statically PlotGGraph().
code: # Construct sample-specific igraph object graph = BuildGraph(   sample.id = "Sample_1",   interactions = results$interactions,   snv.matrix = snv,   cnv.matrix = cnv,   tumor.id = "Tumor",   top.n = 100 )  # Plot interactive cell-cell network PlotVisNetwork(graph, top.n = 100) # Plot static network highlighting Tumor and IL6 signaling PlotGGraph(   graph = graph,   interactions = results$interactions,   highlight.cell = "Tumor",   highlight.gene = "IL6",   top.n = 100 )

what: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: INTERACT (INTEgrative Analysis Cellular Tumor interactions) R package inferring prioritizing cell-cell communication networks within tumor microenvironment. integrating transcriptomic profiles across distinct cell populations downstream pathway activity, lineage-constrained phenotypic programs, optional tumor somatic alterations, INTERACT computes multi-layered communication score candidate ligand-receptor pairs.

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: Standard cell-cell communication inference methods estimate signaling potential primarily co-expression ligand receptor mRNA transcripts. co-expression provides essential baseline, transcript abundance alone indicate whether signal functionally received target cell whether tumor-specific genomic alterations reshaping signaling axis. INTERACT extends co-expression analysis integrating three complementary layers biological evidence: Transcriptional Co-expression (\(S_{\text{base}}\)): Quantifies baseline signaling potential sender ligand receiver receptor expression across single-cell pseudobulk bulk RNA-seq profiles. Downstream Functional Activity (\(W_{\text{pathway}}\) \(W_{\text{program}}\)): Evaluates whether canonical intracellular signaling pathways lineage-matched phenotypic gene programs associated engaged receptor ligand active communicating cells. Tumor Genomic Context (\(W_{\text{genomic}}\)): tumor somatic single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) copy number variants (CNVs) provided, INTERACT adjusts tumor-involved interactions reflect copy number amplifications, single-copy losses, activating loss--function mutations, homozygous deletions. Importantly, genomic alterations treated context-dependent modifiers rather prerequisites. Immune--immune interactions diploid, wild-type tumor interactions neutral genomic modifier (\(W_{\text{genomic}} = 0\)) prioritized strength transcriptional expression functional pathway/program engagement.

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: INTERACT operates additively log space. given sample, sender population, receiver population, ligand-receptor pair, integrated communication score (\(S_{\text{final}}\)) defined : \[S_{\text{final}} = S_{\text{base}} + W_{\text{pathway}} + W_{\text{program}} + W_{\text{genomic}}\]

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: \[S_{\text{base}} = E_{\text{ligand}} + E_{\text{receptor}}\] \(E_{\text{ligand}}\) \(E_{\text{receptor}}\) represent log-scale expression values (e.g., \(\log_2(\text{CPM} + 1)\)) sender receiver populations, respectively. inputs log-transformed, sum corresponds log product linear transcript abundances. Minimum Expression Threshold: ligand receptor must meet minimum expression threshold (min.expression, default = \(1.0\)) interaction evaluated. Multimeric Complexes: Heteromeric ligands receptors (e.g., IL6R_IL6ST) evaluated using minimum expression across constituent subunits, reflecting stoichiometric limiting component.

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: Intracellular pathway activity receiver population inferred using PROGENy across 14 canonical signaling pathways. receptor mapped corresponding downstream pathway(s), \(P_{\text{receiver}}\) defined maximum activity score among pathways linked receptor. prevent extreme outliers dominating score, pathway activity scaled bounded using hyperbolic tangent function: \[W_{\text{pathway}} = \beta_{\text{pathway}} \cdot \tanh\left(\frac{P_{\text{receiver}}}{c_{\text{pathway}}}\right)\] \(\beta_{\text{pathway}}\) (default = \(5\)) sets maximum magnitude (\(\log_2\) expression units) unilateral receiver pathway activation can add subtract \(S_{\text{base}}\). \(c_{\text{pathway}}\) (scale.pathways) data-driven normalization constant automatically calibrated half 95th percentile (\(Q_{0.95} / 2\)) absolute pathway scores across cohort. \(\tanh(2) \approx 0.964\), maps 95% biological variation smoothly onto responsive \((-0.96, +0.96)\) region \(\tanh\) saturating extreme outliers \(\pm 1.0\).

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: Broader cellular states biological processes quantified per cell population using single-sample Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (ssGSEA) across curated gene sets ImmPort, Reactome, Gene Ontology. Gene sets filtered cell lineage compatibility lineage-restricted programs (e.g., TCR signaling BCR signaling) evaluated appropriate populations. sender program score (\(G_{\text{sender}}\)) receiver program score (\(G_{\text{receiver}}\)) bounded jointly: \[W_{\text{program}} = \beta_{\text{program}} \cdot \tanh\left(\frac{G_{\text{sender}} + G_{\text{receiver}}}{c_{\text{program}}}\right)\] \(\beta_{\text{program}}\) (default = \(8\)) sets maximum magnitude bilateral program enrichment across sender receiver compartments (\(\sim 4\) \(\log_2\) units per compartment). \(c_{\text{program}}\) (scale.programs) automatically calibrated \(Q_{0.95} / 2\) combined program scores across cohort.

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: snv.matrix /cnv.matrix supplied, genomic alterations evaluated interactions sender /receiver tumor population (non-tumor populations default wild-type \(\text{SNV} = 0\) diploid \(\text{CNV} = 2.0\)): Homozygous Deletion Filter: tumor exhibits homozygous deletion (\(\text{CNV} < 0.5\)) subunit ligand (tumor sender) receptor (tumor receiver), interaction edge removed prior scoring. Additive Genomic Weight: retained interactions, SNV CNV effects computed : \[W_{\text{genomic,sender}} = \text{SNV}_{\text{sender}} + \tanh\left[\log_2\left(\frac{\max(\text{CNV}_{\text{sender}}, 0.5)}{2.0}\right)\right]\] \[W_{\text{genomic,receiver}} = \text{SNV}_{\text{receiver}} + \tanh\left[\log_2\left(\frac{\max(\text{CNV}_{\text{receiver}}, 0.5)}{2.0}\right)\right]\] \[W_{\text{genomic}} = W_{\text{genomic,sender}} + W_{\text{genomic,receiver}}\] somatic SNVs encoded directionally (\(+1\) activating expression-enhancing alterations, \(-1\) repressive loss--function alterations, \(0\) wild type) copy numbers evaluated relative diploid baseline \(2.0\).

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: Mass-Action Approximation: Baseline interaction potential assumes signaling likelihood scales availability ligand receptor transcripts (\(E_{\text{ligand}} + E_{\text{receptor}}\)). Transcriptomic Proxy: mRNA expression serves surrogate surface protein abundance, transcriptional footprint signatures (PROGENy ssGSEA) serve surrogates downstream signaling engagement. Microenvironmental Co-localization: Sender receiver populations profiled within sample assumed capable paracrine juxtacrine communication within tissue compartment.

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: INTERACT integrates three curated knowledge bases support functional scoring: OmniPath database: Provides reference intercellular communication network (intercell_network(high_confidence = TRUE)). INTERACT filters database via filter_intercell_network() retain curated interactions meeting four criteria: Transmitter topology: ligand/sender molecule must secreted (sec), plasma membrane transmembrane (pmtm), plasma membrane peripheral (pmp), capturing soluble paracrine factors cell-surface contact ligands. Receiver topology: receptor/target molecule must plasma membrane transmembrane (pmtm) protein capable transducing extracellular signals across cell membrane. Literature support: interaction must supported least two independent primary literature references (min_references = 2). Subunit mappability: required gene symbols—including every constituent subunit heteromeric complexes (COMPLEX:)—must measured input expression matrices. PROGENy pathways: Infers activity 14 canonical intracellular signaling pathways (e.g., JAK-STAT, NFkB, TGFb, TNFa, MAPK, PI3K) consensus downstream target gene footprints. INTERACT maps pathways upstream initiating receptors interactions - -weighted according downstream pathway activity receiving cell. Curated Phenotypic Gene Sets: Quantifies broader cellular states (e.g., "T-cell Activation", "Phagocytosis", "Antigen Processing Presentation") per cell population using ssGSEA. default, INTERACT uses curated signatures ImmPort, Reactome, Gene Ontology filtered cell-lineage compatibility.

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: Beyond pairwise interaction scoring, INTERACT includes optional deep learning module built PyTorch Geometric analyze patient-level communication architecture across cohort: Multi-Channel Graph Representation: patient’s microenvironment represented directed graph nodes cell populations edges carry 5-channel feature vector decomposing interaction [RNA, Pathway, Program, SNV, CNV] contributions, paired global tumor mutational burden aneuploidy context. Relational Graph Autoencoder (GINEConv): Graph Isomorphism Network Edge features encodes patient’s signaling graph low-dimensional latent representation (embeddings), trained via link reconstruction feature alignment objectives. Patient Subtyping: Low-dimensional embeddings projected 2D space via UMAP (n_neighbors = 15, min_dist = 0.1), unsupervised patient clusters identified using Louvain community detection mutual undirected shared nearest-neighbor (SNN) graph. Path-Integrated Gradients Attribution: Using RunInteractEdgeGradients(), INTERACT computes axiomatic Path-Integrated Gradients along straight-line path zero-edge baseline patient’s communication tensor. quantifies exact contribution every cell-cell axis biological channel (ig_rna, ig_pathway, ig_program, ig_snv, ig_cnv) toward patient cluster assignment.

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: nontumor.matrices: named list numeric matrices (rows = samples, columns = gene symbols) containing log-normalized expression values (e.g., \(\log_2(\text{CPM} + 1)\)) non-tumor cell populations. tumor.matrix: (Optional) numeric matrix (rows = samples, columns = gene symbols) containing log-normalized gene expression tumor population. snv.matrix: (Optional) numeric matrix (rows = samples, columns = gene symbols) encoding tumor somatic mutations (+1 = activating/expression-enhancing, -1 = repressive/inactivating, 0 = wild type). cnv.matrix: (Optional) numeric matrix (rows = samples, columns = gene symbols) containing absolute continuous gene-level copy number estimates centered 2.0 (diploid). program.gene.lists: (Optional) data.frame mapping functional programs database identifiers (program.name, id, source, url, count). Defaults package’s internal curated gene sets NULL.

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
code: library(INTERACT)  # 1. Run the INTERACT pipeline results = RunInteract(   nontumor.matrices = nontumor.mats,   tumor.matrix = tumor.mat,   snv.matrix = snv.mat,   cnv.matrix = cnv.mat,   run.autoencoder = TRUE,   conda.env = "pytorch",   n.cores = 4 )  # 2. Inspect scored interactions and diagnostic summaries head(results$interactions) names(results$diagnostics)  # 3. Build a sample-specific communication graph graph = BuildGraph(   sample.id = "Patient_01",   interactions = results$interactions,   snv.matrix = snv.mat,   cnv.matrix = cnv.mat,   tumor.id = "Tumor",   top.n = 100 )  # 4. Visualize the network (static ggraph or interactive visNetwork) PlotGGraph(   graph = graph,   interactions = results$interactions,   highlight.cell = "Tumor",   top.n = 100 )  PlotVisNetwork(graph, top.n = 100)  # 5. Launch the interactive Shiny dashboard for cohort-wide exploration LaunchInteractApp(results = results)

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: RunInteract() returns named list containing following objects:

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: data.frame scored ligand-receptor interactions across cohort: source_genesymbol / target_genesymbol: Gene symbols ligand receptor (underscore-delimited subunits complexes). ligand.axis / receptor.axis: Functional classification mapped OmniPath (e.g., checkpoint, cytokine, chemokine, growth_factor). sample: Sample identifier. sender / receiver: Sending receiving cell populations. base.score: Baseline co-expression score (\(S_{\text{base}} = E_{\text{ligand}} + E_{\text{receptor}}\)). s.snv / r.snv: Raw directional somatic SNV states sender receiver (\(+1\), \(-1\), \(0\)). s.cnv / r.cnv: Raw gene-level copy number values sender receiver (\(2.0\) = diploid baseline). weight.pathways: Additive pathway modifier (\(W_{\text{pathway}}\)). weight.programs: Joint additive phenotypic program modifier (\(W_{\text{program}}\)), along proportional diagnostic splits (weight.sender.programs, weight.receiver.programs). weight.genomic: Total additive genomic modifier (\(W_{\text{genomic}}\)), along compartmental splits (weight.sender.genomic, weight.receiver.genomic). Equals \(0\) alteration present non-tumor populations. final.score: Final integrated interaction score (\(S_{\text{final}} = S_{\text{base}} + W_{\text{pathway}} + W_{\text{program}} + W_{\text{genomic}}\)).

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: list summary tables auditing data coverage layer behavior: input.signal: Summarizes input matrix (modality, samples, features, pct.zero, pct.low, median.value). weight.layers: Percentage cohort interactions modified layer (pct.pathway.weighted, pct.program.weighted, pct.genomic.weighted, pct..weighted). receiver.source & sender.source: Counts (n) percentages (pct) interactions stratified combination active functional genomic layers receiver sender compartments. weight.direction: Counts interactions per receiver population Boosted (\(S_{\text{final}} - S_{\text{base}} > 0.01\)), Suppressed (\(S_{\text{final}} - S_{\text{base}} < -0.01\)), Neutral. rank.shift: Summarizes functional genomic weights reorder interaction priorities within sample relative raw co-expression (mean.rank.shift, mean.abs.rank.shift, pct.shifted). mean.layer.weights: Mean additive contribution Pathways, Programs, Genomics across receiver populations. genomic.hits: Aggregates interactions directly modified tumor SNVs CNVs (impacted, alteration.type, n.samples, mean.base.score, mean.final.score). calibration.parameters: Stores cohort-calibrated scaling denominators (scale.pathways, scale.programs).

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: embeddings: data.frame containing latent patient embeddings (GNN.Dim.1 GNN.Dim.N) learned multi-channel Graph Autoencoder (NULL run.autoencoder = FALSE). edge.gradients: data.frame Path-Integrated Gradients attributions quantifying importance cell-cell axis biological channel (ig_score, ig_rna, ig_pathway, ig_program, ig_snv, ig_cnv) patient cluster.

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: list three data.frame objects quantifying network structure across top quartile communication edges per sample: node: Cell-type centrality metrics per sample (degree, strength, betweenness, pagerank, hub.score, authority.score, transitivity.barrat, signaling role category: "Sender", "Receiver", "Mediator", "Influencer"). edge: Aggregated cross-population edge weights (sum.score) edge.betweenness per sample. graph: Sample-level global network properties (density, transitivity.global, transitivity.barrat.mean).

title: INTEgrative Analysis for Cellular and Tumor Interactions
text: precompute: Precomputed tables, UMAP/PCA coordinates, multi-resolution Louvain/k-means clusterings used LaunchInteractApp(). modality.progeny.scores: List sample--pathway PROGENy activity matrices per cell population. functional.program.scores: List sample--program ssGSEA enrichment matrices per cell population. program.gene.lists: Reference gene set table used execution.

title: Run INTERACT Signaling Detection — RunInteract
text: function executes core signaling pipeline INTERACT package, integrating genomic alterations, pathway activity, phenotypic states.

title: Run INTERACT Signaling Detection — RunInteract
code: RunInteract(   nontumor.matrices,   tumor.matrix = NULL,   snv.matrix = NULL,   cnv.matrix = NULL,   program.gene.lists = NULL,   n.cores = max(1, parallelly::availableCores() - 2),   beta.pathways = 5,   beta.programs = 8,   scale.pathways = "auto",   scale.programs = "auto",   pathway.receptor.map = NULL,   program.constraints = NULL,   omni.network = NULL,   min.expression = 1,   calibrate.n.samples = 15,   run.autoencoder = TRUE,   conda.env = "pytorch",   autoencoder.epochs = 150L )

title: Run INTERACT Signaling Detection — RunInteract
text: nontumor.matrices named list expression matrices (samples x features) microenvironment cells. tumor.matrix Optional. single expression matrix tumor cells. snv.matrix Optional. numeric matrix (samples x features) tumor somatic mutations (e.g., 1 = activating, -1 = repressive, 0 = WT). Continuous probabilities also supported. cnv.matrix Optional. matrix (samples x features) tumor copy number alterations (absolute encoding, diploid = 2). program.gene.lists Data frame containing gene sets (ImmPort/Reactome). n.cores Integer. Number cores parallel processing. beta.pathways Numeric. Weighting factor pathway activity. Default 5. beta.programs Numeric. Weighting factor phenotypic programs. Default 8. scale.pathways Numeric "auto". Automatically tuning denominator bring raw PROGENy scores roughly [-2, 2] range squashing. scale.programs Numeric "auto". Automatically tuning denominator bring raw ssGSEA scores roughly [-2, 2] range squashing. pathway.receptor.map Optional custom mapping pathways receptors. program.constraints Optional data frame lineage-specific program filtering. omni.network Optional OmniPath network data frame bypass API download. min.expression Numeric. Minimum log-scale expression threshold ligand receptor subunits. calibrate.n.samples Integer. Number random samples profile auto-calibration. Default 15. run.autoencoder Logical. TRUE, trains multi-channel GNN Graph Autoencoder interaction network extracts latent patient embeddings downstream UMAP Louvain clustering. Default TRUE. conda.env String. Conda environment containing PyTorch PyTorch Geometric autoencoder. Default "pytorch". autoencoder.epochs Integer. Number training epochs Graph Autoencoder. Default 150.

title: Run INTERACT Signaling Detection — RunInteract
text: list containing interactions, diagnostics, embeddings, precompute data, topology metrics.

title: Run INTERACT Signaling Detection — RunInteract
text: Outputs list data frames: interactions: data frame scored cell-cell interactions. Key columns include source_genesymbol (ligand), target_genesymbol (receptor), sample, sender, receiver, base.score (raw expression product), weight.genomic (DNA alteration modifier), weight.pathways (PROGENy modifier), weight.programs (phenotypic modifier), final.score (fully integrated score). diagnostics: list summary data frames auditing pipeline. Includes input.signal (raw matrix summaries), weight.layers (global impact weights), receiver.source sender.source (evidence breakdown), weight.direction (net functional multiplier direction), rank.shift (rank changes weighting), genomic.hits (genomically boosted interactions). topology.metrics: list network metrics calculated per sample. Includes node (centrality signaling roles per cell type), edge (communication weights populations), graph (ecosystem-wide density transitivity). Additional Outputs: precompute (data Shiny app), modality.progeny.scores (raw pathway scores), functional.program.scores (raw program scores), program.gene.lists (reference gene lists).

title: Compute GNN Edge Integrated Gradients — RunInteractEdgeGradients
text: Trains multi-channel Graph Autoencoder (GINEConv) patient microenvironment networks computes path-integrated gradients (attribution scores) cell-cell interaction respect cluster centroids latent embedding space. quantifies exact contribution biological communication channel (RNA, Reactome pathways, PROGENy programs, somatic SNVs, CNVs) toward shaping patient cluster.
